title: Rename Index
description: Learn how to rename an index using sp_rename and SQL Server Management Studio.

data.text: You can rename an index using the system stored procedure sp_rename or through SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS).

data.title: Rename index using sp_rename
data.content: Renames an index from ix_customers_city to ix_cust_city.

data.title: Rename with explicit parameters
data.content: Renames an index using fully qualified object name.

data.text: In SQL Server Management Studio, navigate to the table's Indexes node, right-click the index you want to rename, and select Rename. Then type the new name and press Enter.

When renaming an index, `sp_rename` expects the current object name to be scoped as `schema.table.index`, and it prints a warning that renaming an object can break scripts and stored procedures. The script below renames an index on a real table.

data.title: Rename an index safely
data.content: The first argument can be positional or named; the object type must be `INDEX`. Run against an existing table and index.

data.title: Renames break plan guides and scripts
data.text: sp_rename only changes the name in metadata — any query hints, plan guides, maintenance scripts, or deployment files that reference the old name will fail or silently fall back to a scan. Search the codebase for the old name before renaming in production.

data.title: Rename Index Key Points
points: Use sp_rename with the 'INDEX' object type to rename an index via T-SQL.
You can also rename indexes through SSMS by right-clicking and selecting Rename.
Always specify the schema-qualified table name when using sp_rename.
Renaming an index does not affect its functionality.
